records.issue_text: Host format regex anchored with \A/\Z instead of \z, allowing a host value ending in newline followed by malicious content to bypass validation
records.rationale: In the new model `EmbeddableHost` the host validation regex is `/\A...\Z/i` (see `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`). In Ruby, `\Z` allows a trailing newline, so a value like `"example.com\n"` can pass validation. records.issue_text: Controller destroy action calls host.destroy without checking host is present, causing a 500 error instead of a graceful error for non-existent id
records.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy`. If no record exists for the given `id`, `host` will be `nil` and `nil.destroy` will raise, resulting in a 500 instead of a handled 404/JSON error.

records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost regex allows a path suffix to remain in host after trimming, risking unvalidated path data being used in security-relevant host_allowed? checks
records.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `before_validation` explicitly strips any path suffix via `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`, so a path will not remain in `host` after trimming. Additionally, the security-relevant check `host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which parses the referer with `URI(...)` and uses `uri.host` (hostname only), so path data is not used in the allowlist lookup at all.
